subject.title: Feature request: Add Gateway received timestamp to inbound metadata for accurate latency tracking

question: What exact cross-channel receipt-time contract should OpenClaw expose to agents for inbound messages?
rationale: The source path is clear, but adding the field defines agent-visible API semantics across channels and prompt-cache boundaries; automation should not choose the permanent field name, format, or metadata placement without maintainer intent.

options.title: Add volatile per-turn field
options.body: Expose a single ISO or millisecond Gateway receipt timestamp in the user-role conversation metadata while keeping trusted system metadata stable; this best matches the current prompt-cache boundary.

options.title: Keep timing internal for now
options.body: Leave `receivedAt` only in receive queues/logs and solve latency diagnostics through logs or diagnostics exports instead of model-visible metadata.

options.title: Design broader stage timing
options.body: Defer this field to a larger per-stage timing contract covering receipt, agent start, first token, and outbound send across supported channels.

recommendation.title: Add volatile per-turn field
recommendation.body: Expose a single ISO or millisecond Gateway receipt timestamp in the user-role conversation metadata while keeping trusted system metadata stable; this best matches the current prompt-cache boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans channel SDK contracts, prompt metadata, and cache-stability policy, and this handle has adjacent SDK/channel contract history.
